title: Connect graph vertex deletion to list-CNF assignment semantics
claim: For a finite simple graph G on Fin n, a vertex v and a Nat-indexed Boolean assignment a, the selected theorem proves that evaluating the positive edge CNF after setting a(v) to true equals evaluating the original assignment on the edge CNF with every edge incident to v removed. The CNF uses the protocol list evaluator: each edge contributes a positive two-literal clause. This supplies an explicit compatibility statement between the upstream graph restriction lemma and the local CNF representation.
novelty: The upstream L_meta_253 already describes how a graph edge predicate changes when a vertex input is set to false. The local proof adds a graph-relation-to-list-CNF definition, proves the semantics of its positive clauses, proves the complement relation with the upstream predicate, and proves that updating the Nat assignment commutes with complementing its restriction to Fin n. It then uses L_meta_253 to obtain graphCNF_delete_vertex. This is new integration work in this packet, not a new graph-theoretic result or a claim of global novelty.

limitations: The compatibility theorem concerns positive two-literal edge CNFs from finite simple graphs, not arbitrary CNFs. Both edge orientations appear, so clauses can be duplicated; the semantics proof accounts for that representation. The definition uses noncomputable Finset.toList and does not provide an executable or efficient graph-conversion service. It reproduces five protocol evaluator definitions inside the artifact, rather than importing a previously credited research theorem. No new complexity bound, toolchain migration, full P-versus-NP result or comprehensive novelty search is claimed.
